26 (Currently amended): A non-transitory machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document, the document having a drawing order that indicates the order in which the primitive graphic elements are drawn when the document is displayed; calculating a first value for a first primitive graphic element and a second primitive graphic element that is subsequent to the first in the drawing order, wherein the first value represents a size value that does not necessarily equate to a character size or spacing value; and based on the comparison of the first value to other values calculated for additional primitive graphic elements that are subsequent in the drawing order, defining a single structural graphic element within the document from the first and second primitive graphic elements.

27 (Original): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the first value is a size value.

28 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the first value represents a size of a smallest bounding box that encompasses the first and second primitive graphic elements, wherein the size is not limited to character sizes described in other references.

31 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the set of instructions for calculating comprises a set of instructions for calculating a different value for each pair of primitive graphic elements subsequent in the drawing order, wherein the set of instructions for defining the single structural graphic element comprises sets of instructions for: using the calculated values for pairs of primitive graphic elements to identify clusters of primitive graphic elements as candidates for joining as compound graphic elements; and identifying sequences of primitive graphic elements within a cluster whose bounding boxes intersect; and joining the sequences as single graphic elements, wherein this identification and joining process is not limited to bounding box overlaps specifically described in Mansfield.

32 (Currently amended): A non-transitory machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document; based on values calculated for pairs of primitive graphic elements, defining a set of successive primitive graphic elements as a candidate compound graphic element, wherein this candidate definition is not algorithmically constrained by prior art descriptions; using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements within the set; and defining each particular subset having more than one primitive graphic element as a single structural graphic element within the document, the structural graphic element comprising the primitive graphic elements in the particular subset.

33 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 32, wherein the set of instructions for defining the set of successive primitive graphic elements comprises performing cluster analysis on the calculated values, whereby this analysis approach does not strictly adhere to traditional analysis boundaries.

41 (Currently amended): The method of claim 37, wherein the calculating comprises calculating a different value for each pair of primitive graphic elements subsequent in the drawing order, wherein defining the single structural graphic element comprises: using the calculated values for pairs of primitive graphic elements to identify clusters of primitive graphic elements as candidates for joining as compound graphic elements; and identifying sequences of primitive graphic elements within a cluster whose bounding boxes intersect; and joining the sequences as single graphic elements, with no limitation to the exact definitions previously outlined in Mansfield.

42 (Currently amended): An apparatus comprising: a set of processing units; and a machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document; based on values calculated for pairs of primitive graphic elements, defining a set of successive primitive graphic elements as a candidate compound graphic element, whereby this definition is not strictly synonymous with prior art disclosures; using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements within the set; and defining each particular subset having more than one primitive graphic element as a single structural graphic element within the document, the structural graphic element comprising the primitive graphic elements in the particular subset.
